title: Turbulent channel flow validation vs KMM1987 DNS (Re_tau=180)
summary: SST reproduces the mean velocity u+(y+) of the imported low-Re channel DNS over the literal anchor window y+ in [30, centreline] with 3.46 % RMS relative error at 256 cells, but 6.12 % over the physical log layer y+ in [30, 0.2 Re_tau] = [30, 36.4]; the 5 % criterion therefore holds only under the legacy (diluted) window. k-omega and k-epsilon fail both windows (10.6 % / 6.8 % legacy). See grading_windows for both numbers.
dns_proxy: Lee & Moser 2015 JFM 774:395 (Re_tau=182.088). Substitution cost measured, not assumed, and now measured on every driver run across the five quoted cases: they are re-solved at the reference Re_tau and the delta on both grading windows is recorded in docs/case-fvm-channel-kmm180/benchmark.json -> reference_substitution. Measured maximum 0.097 pp (sst n=64, legacy window) / 0.078 pp (sst n=64, log layer); every delta is below 0.04 pp for n>=128; no verdict flips. The 0.02 pp figure quoted by docs/verification-channel-kmm180-loglaw/REPORT.md section 3.3 is that same quantity at n=256 only, so this entry no longer states it as a grid-independent bound.
method: 1-D equilibrium channel solver with SST/k-omega/k-epsilon turbulence models
verdict: QUALIFIED: PASS under the legacy window y+ in [30, centreline]; FAIL under the physical log layer y+ in [30, 0.2 Re_tau]. Both numbers are published below and neither may be quoted alone.

legacy_full.definition: y+ in [30, centreline (180.56 at Re_tau=182.088)]; the literal reading of the anchor text
legacy_full.caveat: an outer-layer denominator (mean u+ 18.4 vs 16.3 in the log layer) dilutes a near-constant u+ offset; this window can pass without the log layer being reproduced

log_layer.caveat: at Re_tau=182 the physical log layer is only ~6 wall units wide, so this window is itself a compromise; the DNS deviates 3.04 % from the classic log law (kappa=0.41, B=5.2) over the same interval

acceptance_criterion: RMS relative deviation of u+(y+) in y+>30 region < 5%

critique.is_the_failure_a_solver_defect: No. Three independent checks. (a) Momentum identity: with unit friction velocity the equilibrium shear balance implies dU+/dln y+ = y+(1 - y/h)/(1 + nu_t+/nu), so the profile's log slope is predicted by the turbulence state alone; measured vs predicted kappa agrees to 0.029 % (SST) and 0.001 % (k-omega), i.e. no momentum-flux bookkeeping error -- the u+ deficit is carried entirely by nu_t. (b) At Re_tau=182 the state sits at kappa_eddy = nu_t+/y+ = 0.204 (SST) against the model's own closed-form kappa = 0.408; both k+ and kappa_eddy rise monotonically towards the closed-form values as Re_tau grows (k+ 2.67 -> 2.97 against 1/sqrt(beta*) = 3.333 from Re_tau 550 to 5200, kappa_eddy 0.285 -> 0.342 against 0.408). (c) Predicting k+ with the window-mean total-stress factor (1 - y/h) leaves a residual falling from 9.4 % to 3.3 %: the shortfall is the finite-domain (1 - y/h) factor plus a non-asymptotic y+=30, not bookkeeping.
critique.reference_substitution_bound: Measured, not assumed, and measured on every driver run: the quoted cases (sst 64/128/256, k-omega 128, k-epsilon 128) are re-solved at Re_tau=182.088 and the RMS delta on both windows is recorded in benchmark.json -> reference_substitution. Max delta 0.097 pp (legacy) / 0.078 pp (log layer), both at n=64 (the coarse grid); <=0.04 pp for n>=128; verdict flips: none. Cf and U_bulk+ move by <=0.50 % / <=0.26 %. The n=256-only measurement in docs/verification-channel-kmm180-loglaw/REPORT.md section 3.3 (0.02 pp) is consistent with this but is not a grid-independent bound. The artifact gate (scripts/run_case_fvm_channel_kmm180.py --check) fails if the measured delta exceeds the pre-declared 0.15 pp band or if a verdict flips.

repro_cmd: PYTHONPATH=src python -m tensorfvm.benchmark_channel_kmm1987 --out docs/case-fvm-channel-kmm180   # or: PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/run_case_fvm_channel_kmm180.py --run
test_cmd: PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_channel_kmm180_artifacts.py tests/test_channel_kmm180_loglaw.py tests/test_channel_kmm180_windows.py tests/test_channel_kmm1987.py -q
notes: k-omega and k-epsilon have known biases in the log region; SST is the best of the three models at this Re_tau but still misses the physical log layer. The reference is a documented proxy (KMM1987 -> Lee & Moser 2015) whose cost is re-measured on every driver run (max 0.097 pp at n=64, no verdict flips) and gated against a pre-declared 0.15 pp band, rather than asserted. Artifacts: docs/case-fvm-channel-kmm180/{benchmark.json, metrics.csv, profiles.csv, stations.csv} are machine-written and cross-checked by the gate; manifest.json pins their sha256.
artifact_gate_cmd: PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/run_case_fvm_channel_kmm180.py --check   # offline cross-check of artifacts, manifest sha256 and this entry
